For (u,v)≠(0,0) the last equation is always a nonzero linear constraint on (b,e,B,E), giving an affine bundle of relative dimension three there, plus two central free coordinates. This gives a geometrically irreducible dimension-nine fiber of class (L²−1)L⁷. For u=v=0, let Z be d=D=0. For w≠0 the patch off Z has class (L²−1)²L⁵, and Z has class (L⁴−1)L⁵: remove the vanishing coefficient vector of the last linear equation in each case. At w=0 add respectively (L²−1)L⁶ and L⁶. The latter additions total L⁸. For central targets, off Z each d or D chart eliminates the first two equations and reduces the last to a two-pair dot product at level w, primitive linear in one variable and geometrically irreducible in all characteristics. The charts intersect. Z is a four-pair dot-product hypersurface times the two free central coordinates, also geometrically irreducible of dimension nine. The two closed pieces (closure of the open part and Z) cannot contain one another because they have equal dimension and only one lies in d=D=0. The formula at RESULT.md line 63 uses dw rather than w for the coordinates in line 60; multiplying the two tilded coordinates by the unit d gives the stated normalization and does not change the argument.
